To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MCFCs can be used in natural gas fired power plants to achieve high levels of CO2 capture with acceptable energy penalties and CO2 avoidance costs.
the MCFC based CO2 capture process is a very promising solution for natural gas fired power plants.
the MCFC based integrated NGCC configuration shows the best performance in terms of CO2 avoidance cost and energy penalties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) the design of an efficient heat exchanger network for preheating the cathode reactants in the "non integrated configuration"; (ii) the selection of the MCFC operating conditions and the design of the MCFC modules in the "integrated configuration"; (iii) the design and sizing of the MCFC based CO2 purification unit; (iv) the design and selection of the CO2 compression unit; (v) the techno-economic analysis of the proposed schemes
the development of a novel, low energy and low cost process for carbon capture in power plants.
the development of a new technology to produce hydrogen by steam reforming of natural gas and subsequent water gas shift reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "integrated MCFC" scheme is a viable and cost effective solution for the capture of CO2 from natural gas fired power plants.
MCFC technology can be successfully used in NGCC plants to capture CO2 at a cost comparable with that of conventional amine scrubbing processes.
the "integrated configuration" is more attractive than the "non integrated configuration" from both energy and cost points of view, and it is therefore the preferred solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "integrated scheme" is more efficient but requires a higher investment cost, while the "non integrated scheme" is cheaper but requires higher fuel consumption.
the "integrated MCFC" configuration is the most promising option for the capture of CO2 in NGCC power plants.

the integrated MCFC scheme can be considered as a promising alternative for CO2 capture in NGCC plants, with a potential for cost reduction in the range of 20-30% if compared to amine scrubbing processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the considered NGCC power plant (300 MWel), the "integrated MCFC based" scheme can achieve a 20% improvement in the CO2 capture energy efficiency compared to the benchmark process.
the "integrated MCFC" layout is the most promising option for natural gas fired combined power plants for CO2 capture.
the integration of MCFC in NGCC plants is a promising technology for the capture of CO2 from power plants, with a strong potential for cost reduction compared to amine based systems.
